issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Issues with using `dataclass_transform` based Declarative mapping on Py `3.10.7`.
In this case, issues with mapped_column being partially undefined.

(note: at some point, it stopped being that error and instead was giving me an error about primary key not being a param, but couldn't repro anymore)

### To Reproduce

Full test case:

```python
# isort:skip
# pylint:disable = unused-import, too-few-public-methods, missing-class-docstring

# Inferred issues
#       Type of "mapped_column" is partially unknown
#       Type of "mapped_column" is "(__name_pos: str | Type[TypeEngine[Any]] | TypeEngine[Any] | SchemaEventTarget | None = None, __type_pos: Type[TypeEngine[Any]] | TypeEngine[Any] | SchemaEventTarget | None = None, *args: SchemaEventTarget, init: _NoArg | bool = _NoArg.NO_ARG, repr: _NoArg | bool = _NoArg.NO_ARG, default: Any | None = _NoArg.NO_ARG, default_factory: _NoArg | (() -> _T@mapped_column) = _NoArg.NO_ARG, kw_only: _NoArg | bool = _NoArg.NO_ARG, nullable: bool | Literal[SchemaConst.NULL_UNSPECIFIED] | None = SchemaConst.NULL_UNSPECIFIED, primary_key: bool | None = False, deferred: _NoArg | bool = _NoArg.NO_ARG, deferred_group: str | None = None, deferred_raiseload: bool = False, name: str | None = None, type_: Type[TypeEngine[Any]] | TypeEngine[Any] | None = None, autoincrement: bool | Literal['auto', 'ignore_fk'] = "auto", doc: str | None = None, key: str | None = None, index: bool | None = None, unique: bool | None = None, info: Dict[Any, Any] | None = None, onupdate: Any | None = None, insert_default: Any | None = _NoArg.NO_ARG, server_default: FetchedValue | str | TextClause | ColumnElement[Unknown] | None = None, server_onupdate: FetchedValue | None = None, quote: bool | None = None, system: bool = False, comment: str | None = None, **dialect_kwargs: Any) -> MappedColumn[Any]"
#       Pylance reportUnknownVariableType
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, MappedAsDataclass, mapped_column

# Inferred issues
#   "dataclass_transform" is not accessed Pylance
from typing_extensions import dataclass_transform  # type: ignore


class BaseEntity(MappedAsDataclass, DeclarativeBase):
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(init=False, primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(init=True)


# Inferred as by Intellisense:
#   (class) BaseEntity(name: SQLCoreOperations[str] | str)
# Inferred errors:
#   Argument missing for parameter "name" Pylance reportGeneralTypeIssues
BaseEntity()


# Inferred as by Intellisense:
#   (class) BaseEntity(name: SQLCoreOperations[str] | str)
#   non_existing: Unknown
# Inferred errors:
#   Argument missing for parameter "name" Pylance reportGeneralTypeIssues
#   No parameter named "non_existing" Pylance reportGeneralTypeIssues
BaseEntity(non_existing=42)


# Inferred as by Intellisense:
#   (class) BaseEntity(name: SQLCoreOperations[str] | str)
BaseEntity(name="Hello")
```


### Error

Errors + reports are included inline for easier reference

### Versions

- OS: Win 11
- Python: Python 3.10.7
- sqlalchemy = "2.0.0b1"
- Database: N/A
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): N/A


### Additional context

Related to Beta #8631

body:
It seems that a classmethod is not considered a ClassVar by pylance.
using as type information `ClassVar[Any] | classmethod[Any]` seems to work.

Not sure if it's expected or not.

The `ClassVar[Any] | classmethod[Any]` is not liked by mypy, that will error with
```
test1.py:50: error: Invalid type: ClassVar nested inside other type  [misc]
test1.py:55: error: Signature of "Bar" incompatible with supertype "Foo"  [override]
```
Also I found this issue on Pylance https://github.com/microsoft/pylance-release/issues/2129.
it does not seem relevant since that's probably using 1.4 where the types were very different

issue.title: Is a classmethod a classvar?
issue.body:
Hi

as per title, is a classmethod considered a classvar?
In particular if it can override a variable defined a classvar in a supertype, since pylance, pyright and mypy seem to have differing opinions in this regard.

The following example type checks fine in mypy and pyright 
```py
from typing import Any, ClassVar

class Foo:
    Bar: ClassVar[Any]

class Baz(Foo):
    @classmethod
    def Bar(cls) -> int:
        return 42

class FooBar(Foo):
    Bar = 42
```
but errors in pylance with 
```
Instance variable "Bar" overrides class variable of same name in class "Foo"Pylance[reportIncompatibleVariableOverride](https://github.com/microsoft/pylance-release/blob/main/DIAGNOSTIC_SEVERITY_RULES.md#diagnostic-severity-rules)
```

Adding classmethod  to the Bar definition works for pylance and pyright
```py
from typing import Any, ClassVar

class Foo:
    Bar: ClassVar[Any] | classmethod[Any]

class Baz(Foo):
    @classmethod
    def Bar(cls) -> int:
        return 42

class FooBar(Foo):
    Bar = 42
```
but errors in mypy with
```
error: Invalid type: ClassVar nested inside other type  [misc]
error: Signature of "Bar" incompatible with supertype "Foo"  [override]
```

Context for this question is [`__tablename__` in sqlalchemy](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/c97ab04e0138a9e1fb612938047cf337dc1ec100/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/decl_api.py#L688), that's currently typed as `ClassVar[Any]` but that's not liked by pylance.
This is the original issue reported to sqlalchemy https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/8645

cc @zzzeek

```
[tool.pyright]
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = false
````
